# ait

> AI coding agents should work in attempts, not your working tree. ait turns Claude Code, Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini CLI, and Cursor runs into isolated, reviewable attempts with provenance, shared long-term repo memory, cross-agent handoff, adversarial review, and explicit apply/recover flow on top of Git. Open source (MIT), Python 3.14+, dependency-free, no SaaS, no telemetry. Metadata is stored locally under `.ait/` next to `.git/`. The package is named `ait-vcs` on PyPI and npm; the installed command is `ait`.

ait is not an agent and not a Git replacement. It is the local attempt workflow around AI coding agents. Every wrapped agent run produces one "attempt" record linking intent -> prompt -> context files -> exit status -> edited files -> resulting commits, queryable via a structured DSL. `ait status <adapter>` reports wrapper bypass risk so users can see whether the current shell will enter AIT or silently call the real agent binary. Repo-local memory imports prior attempts, prior commits, curated notes, accepted facts, prior findings, and agent memory files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) under local policy, then recalls only allowed context into `AIT_CONTEXT_FILE` for the next run. `ait memory backfill --dry-run` previews existing repo-local agent memory without writing; `--import` adds advisory memory under `.ait/`, and global or out-of-repo memory requires an explicit path. Failed attempts stay isolated in their own worktree until you recover or discard them; successful changes only reach the current branch when you call `ait apply`.

## Core docs

- [Home](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/): overview, install, problems solved
- [Why ait](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/why-ait/): the ten problems ait solves (blast radius, provenance, parallel agents, explicit apply, cross-agent handoff, local-first, review evidence, prompt search)
- [Pain-point demos](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/demos/pain-point-demos/): Claude Code and Codex scenario commands for every problem on the Why ait page, including isolation, provenance, context handoff, explicit apply, local-only metadata, review evidence, and prompt search. The repository also provides an executable suite under `examples/pain-point-demos` with `setup.sh` plus one `run.sh` per pain point.
- [Getting started](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/getting-started/): install ait-vcs, run `ait init`, check wrapper bypass status, run first wrapped agent, optionally preview memory backfill, apply the attempt
- [Command reference](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/commands/): all `ait` subcommands — init, status and bypass detection, doctor, adapter, attempt, intent, context, memory and backfill, review, graph, repair, upgrade, shell
- [Review modes](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/review-modes/): exact boundaries for `light`, `adversarial`, `risk-based`, local `claude -p` reviewer execution, and policy-gated memory baselines
- [Adversarial code review](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/reference/adversarial-code-review/): end-to-end reviewer workflow — risk scan, Claude Code reviewer adapter, custom command adapters, findings, reports, and review-gated apply decisions
- [AI search facts](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/facts/): self-contained Q&A — what is ait, how it differs from git-worktree, install, supported agents, privacy, safety guarantees

## Integrations

- [Claude Code](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/claude-code/): wrap `claude` in a worktree; `ait init` auto-installs the wrapper and merges SessionStart/PostToolUse/SessionEnd hooks into `.claude/settings.json`; the `claude-code` adversarial reviewer uses local `claude -p` and strips `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from that child process
- [Codex CLI](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/codex/): native `.codex/hooks.json` bridge with full transcript capture
- [Aider](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/aider/): post-run `.aider.chat.history.md` conversion to attempt transcript
- [Gemini CLI](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/gemini/): native `.gemini/settings.json` hook bridge
- [Cursor](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/cursor/): captures `cursor-agent --print --output-format stream-json` stream
- [Generic shell agent](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/integrations/shell/): `ait run --adapter shell -- <any command>` for custom agents

## Comparisons

- [ait vs naked git-worktree](https://m24927605.github.io/ait/compare/git-worktree-naked-vs-ait/): when manual worktrees suffice and when they break down
